safi-cedvel:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(ذكر) the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هو" (it) or "this" [Note: It may be a postponed mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "among what is recited to you is a mention ..."], (عبده) the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the maṣdar (verbal noun) رحمة, accusative; (زكريّا) an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) — or badal (substitute) — of عبد, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddara) on the alif.
The clause «(هذا) ذكر ...» has no grammatical position, initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
3- (إذ) an adverb of past time attached to (mutaʿalliq) (رحمة) [Note: Al-ʿUkbarī permitted attaching it to ذكر, and that is far-fetched.], (نداء) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative.
The clause «نادى ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

* Morphology:
(خفيّا), an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the triliteral verb خفيّ يخفى, of the pattern-class of fariḥa; its pattern is فعيل, and the yāʾ of فعيل has been assimilated into its third radical.

* Rhetoric:
- Precaution (al-iḥtirās):
In the saying of Allah the Exalted «نِداءً خَفِيًّا».
Iḥtirās means that the speaker brings a meaning against which an objection, ambiguity or false impression could be raised, and he becomes aware of that while composing, so he brings into the body of the speech what frees it from all of that.
In this noble verse, he brought the word خفيّا in keeping with the way (sunna) of Allah in concealing one's supplication, because speaking aloud and concealing are equal before Allah; so it was more fitting for him to guard against what might give the impression of showing off before people.

* Benefits:
- The letters at the beginnings of surahs:
We dealt earlier with what has been said about these letters.
Had there been established for us a text from the hadith or the Qur'an giving us the decisive word on the meanings of these letters, it would have spared us the ijtihād of those who exercise it. As long as we have not come upon a text that relieves us of interpretation and weighing of views, we must affirm what we held in an earlier discussion, which is summed up as follows:
«Since the pronunciation of these letters — kāf, hā, yā, ʿayn, ṣād — is the very spelling pronunciation recognized among the scholars of language, we have only to pursue one of two considerations:
The first: that Allah wills, among what He wills by the message of His Messenger and the sending down of revelation upon him, to teach him and teach us the letters of our language, because of the momentous role of the letters of language in the mission of knowledge and learning and as the means of address and mutual understanding among human beings, which is the fabric that distinguishes man from the other animals.
The second: that these alphabet letters have sanctity and secrets with Allah, as the practitioners of «the great jummal and the small jummal [Translator's note: letter-numerology systems] claim, and whoever follows this approach that resembles magic yet is not magic — that they have such a momentous standing with Allah as makes them the object of His oath and the focus of His concern. And Allah knows best. [Translator's note: the source opens a guillemet «… before "Since" and another before "the great jummal" without closing them.]

safi-cedvel:4-6.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّ) the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, with the vocative particle omitted, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddara) on the letter before the first-person yāʾ, which was dropped for lightness — originally ربّي — and the dropped (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (منّي) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of العظم; (الواو) conjunction in both places; (شيبا) a tamyīz (specification) converted from the agent, accusative; (بدعائك) attached to (شقيّا), and the maṣdar (verbal noun) دعاء has been annexed to its object, i.e. (بدعائي إيّاك) "by my calling on You"; (شقيّا) the khabar (predicate) of أكن, accusative.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «the vocative and its answer ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «إنّي وهن العظم ...» has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative. The clause «وهن العظم ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «اشتعل الرأس ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause وهن العظم [Note: The link is an implied pronoun, i.e. "the head has blazed of me with grey hair".].
The clause «لم أكن.. شقيّا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the answer to the vocative.
The clause «the vocative: ربّ (the second) ...» has no grammatical position, parenthetical.
5- (الواو) conjunction; (من ورائي) attached to a ḥāl of الموالي [Note: It may be attached to الموالي because of the verbal sense in the word, i.e. "those who take charge of the affair after me ..."], (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya) before كانت; (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (هب) an imperative verb of supplication, and the fāʿil (agent) is "You"; (لي) attached to (هب); (من لدنك) attached to (هب); (وليّا) a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative.
The clause «إنّي خفت ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause answering the vocative.
The clause «خفت الموالي ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «كانت امرأتي عاقرا» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, with (قد) understood.
The clause «هب لي ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if this is my state, then grant me".
6- (النون) for protection (wiqāya) in (يرثني); (من آل) attached to (يرث); (رضيّا) a second direct object, accusative.
The clause «يرثني ...» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of (وليّا).
The clause «يرث من آل يعقوب ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause يرثني.
The clause «the vocative: ربّ (the third)» has no grammatical position, parenthetical, to emphasize the plea for mercy.

* Morphology:
(شيبا), an aurally-transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb شاب يشيب, of the pattern-class of ḍaraba; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn; there are other maṣdars: شيبة with fatḥa on the shīn, and مشيب with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the shīn.
(الموالي), plural of مولى, which is the close agnatic relative; a noun whose pattern is مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm and on the second radical.
(رضيّا), an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from رضيّ يرضى, of the pattern-class of fariḥa; its pattern is فعيل, and the yāʾ of فعيل has been assimilated into the third radical, which was originally a wāw, from الرضوان; when the yāʾ and the wāw met with the first vowelless, it was converted into a yāʾ and assimilated into the other yāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
- Metaphor (istiʿāra):
In the saying of Allah the Exalted «اشْتَعَلَ الرَّأْسُ شَيْباً».
He likened the spread of grey hair and its abundance to the blazing of fire in firewood; blazing was borrowed for spreading, and اشتعل was derived from it in the sense of انتشر (it spread). So it contains a consequential metaphor (istiʿāra tabaʿiyya).

* Benefits:
- The role of «grey hair in Arabic literature»: He, Mighty is His affair, described grey hair as blazing; for just as fire is stinging and burning, hurting whoever touches it, so too grey hair hurts the grey-haired. How could it not, when the fair maidens have turned away from him and eyes have scorned him? Ibn al-Rūmī observed that and said: وكنت جلاء للعيون من القذى ... فأصبحت تقذى بشيبي وترمد
(I used to be a cleansing for the eyes from motes — now they are irritated and inflamed by my grey hair;)

هي الأعين النجل التي كنت تشتكي ... مواقعها في القلب والرأس أسود
(they are the same wide eyes whose strikes in the heart you used to complain of, while the head was black.)
And of it is the saying of Abū Tammām:
يا نسيب التغام ذنبك أبقى ... حسناتي عند الحسان ذنوبا
(O kinsman of the white thaghām plant [Translator's note: the source prints «التغام», apparently for «الثغام»], your sin has left my good deeds counted as sins in the eyes of the fair;)

لو رأى الله أن في الشيب خيرا ... جاورته الأبرار في الخلد شيبا
(had Allah seen any good in grey hair, the righteous would dwell near Him in eternity grey-haired.)
And the master of that is ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa, where he said:
رأين الغواني الشيب لاح بعارضي ... فأعرضن عني بالخدور الغواضر
(The beauties saw grey hair appear on my cheek, so they turned their fresh cheeks away from me.)
And may Allah make the soil of Shawqī's grave fragrant, when he sat on the banks of the «Bardūnī» in Zaḥla and listened to the whispering of the jewellery of the fair maidens, and that stirred him, though he was past seventy, and he said:
شيّعت أحلامي بقلب باك ... ولمحت من طرق الملاح شباكي
(I bade farewell to my dreams with a weeping heart, and glimpsed my nets on the paths of the beauties;)

ورجعت أدراج الشباب وورده ... أمشي مكانهما على الأشواك
(and I retraced the steps of youth and its roses, walking in their place upon thorns.)
And in Arabic literature, its poetry and its prose, about grey hair, dyeing, and the white growing out from beneath the black, there is a great deal indeed.

safi-cedvel:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(زكريّا) the one addressed (munādā), a singular proper noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the alif, in the position of accusative; (بغلام) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نبشّرك); (له) attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (قبل) a noun indeclinable on ḍamma in the position of genitive, attached to (سميّا), which is a direct object, accusative.
The clause «the vocative: يا زكريّا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «إنّا نبشّرك ...» has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
The clause «نبشّرك ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of inna.
The clause «اسمه يحيى ...» is in the position of genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of غلام.
The clause «لم نجعل ...» is in the position of genitive as a second adjective of غلام [Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of غلام, because it is qualified.].

* Morphology:
(سميّا), a derived noun whose pattern is فعيل in the sense of مفعول, i.e. "named"; and سمّي contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by conversion: its original form is سميو; the yāʾ and the wāw met with the first vowelless, so the wāw was converted into a yāʾ and assimilated into the other yāʾ.

* Benefits:
1- The noun (al-ism) and its derivation:
In the book al-Inṣāf fī Masāʾil al-Khilāf bayn al-Baṣriyyīn wa-l-Kūfiyyīn there is an interesting discussion about the origin of «الاسم» and its derivation. The upshot of the disagreement is that the Basrans hold that it is derived from «السموّ» (elevation), and the Kufans hold that it is derived from «السمة», which is the mark; on verification, the view of the Basrans is preferable.
سما يسمو سموّا is said when something rises high; it is as if the name is what has risen and become apparent, and so became a sign of the thing named.
So: the noun is a word that indicates the thing named by way of pointing, not of conveying information.
From الاسم are derived أسميت and سمّيت, both transitive to two objects, e.g. سمّيته عليّا (I named him ʿAlī), and it is permissible to put it in the genitive with a preposition. The noun is of two kinds: a concrete noun (ism dhāt): what is coined for a meaning subsisting in itself, such as «زيد»; and an abstract noun (ism maʿnā): what is coined for a meaning subsisting in something else, such as blackness, whiteness, taking, giving, etc. The noun consists of three letters, or four or five; if it is less than three, what is missing has been dropped from it, and if it exceeds five, that is by means of the augment letters, which are not part of the root of the noun. The topic has further aspects, so seek them in the extensive works on grammar and language.
2- We indicated earlier the two adverbs «قبل and بعد» and what is particular to them, and we remind the reader once more that قبل and بعد, when the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) is kept in mind but not mentioned, are indeclinable on ḍamma, e.g.: «وَقَدْ خَلَقْتُكَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَلَمْ تَكُ شَيْئاً», i.e. "before that".

safi-cedvel:8-8.t:
* I'rab:
(أنّى) an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of غلام or of the yāʾ in (لي); and (لي) is attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of يكون; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya) in both places; (من الكبر) attached to (بلغت) [Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl of (عتيّا).], (عتيّا) a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative [Note: Al-ʿUkbarī permitted it to be a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl, i.e. "being extremely aged" or "possessed of extreme age", and to be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar because it coincides with it in meaning, and to be a tamyīz (specification).. All of that is on the assumption that (من) is redundant (zāʾida), which is contrary to what the majority established about the cases in which (من) is redundant.].
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «the vocative: ربّ» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl) [Note: It may be parenthetical, with the clause يكون لي غلام being the speech reported.]. The clause «يكون لي غلام ...» has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
The clause «كانت امرأتي عاقرا ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the yāʾ in (لي).
The clause «بلغت ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, or conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the ḥāl clause.

* Morphology:
(عتيّا), maṣdar of عتا يعتو عتوّا — with ḍamma or kasra on the ʿayn — meaning he grew old.
The word here is with kasra on the ʿayn — which is the reading of Ḥafṣ — and it contains weak-letter changes (iʿlāl) in several respects: its original form is عتوو like قعود; the tāʾ was given kasra for lightness, because of the heaviness of the two ḍammas, so the first wāw was converted into a yāʾ because it was vowelless and the letter before it had kasra, and it became عتيو; then the second wāw was converted into a yāʾ because a yāʾ and a wāw met with the first vowelless, so it became عتيّ with ḍamma on the ʿayn and kasra on the tāʾ; then the ʿayn was given kasra by vowel harmony (li-l-mujāwara), and it became عتيّ.

* Rhetoric:
- Concision (al-ījāz):
In the saying of Allah the Exalted «أَنَّى يَكُونُ لِي غُلامٌ».
Outwardly, the Prophet of Allah Zakariyyā deemed unlikely what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had promised would occur. But it is not permissible for a prophet to utter what is not permissible or what outwardly gives a false impression; so the speech came concise, its implied meaning being: Will our strength and youth be restored to us so that we are granted a boy?! Or will the child be from someone other than the barren wife?

safi-cedvel:9-9.t:
* I'rab:
(كذلك) the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "the matter is thus"; (عليّ) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (هيّن); (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (قبل) a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma in the position of genitive, attached to (خلقتك); (الواو) circumstantial; (تك) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the overt sukūn on the nūn that was dropped for lightness, and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنت" (you); (شيئا) the khabar of تك, accusative.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive [Note: There is disagreement about the agent of the verb: it is said to be Allah, Majestic and Exalted, and it is said to be the angel conveying the glad tidings, namely Jibrīl, peace be upon him, even though he has not been mentioned before.].
The clause «(الأمر) كذلك ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قال ربّك ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive [Note: The clause was repeated for emphasis, as al-Jamal says in his Ḥāshiya.].
The clause «هو عليّ هيّن ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported.
The clause «قد خلقتك ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
The clause «لم تك شيئا ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, or conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the ḥāl clause.

* Morphology:
(هيّن), an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from هان يهون; its pattern is فعيل [Translator's note: so in the source; هيّن is usually given the pattern فيعل.], and it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by conversion: its original form is هيون; the yāʾ met the wāw with the first vowelless, so the wāw was converted into a yāʾ and assimilated into the second yāʾ.

safi-cedvel:10-11.t:
* I'rab:
(لي) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of the verb اجعل; (آية) a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (آيتك) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, with muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle, and (لا) negating; (ثلاث) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (تكلّم); (ليال) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddara) on the yāʾ that was dropped because of the nunation, which is the nunation of compensation (tanwīn al-ʿiwaḍ); (سويّا) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of the verb تكلّم, i.e. "while you are sound, not because of an illness" [Note: If the word refers back to the nights, it is an accusative naʿt (adjective) of (ثلاث ليال).].
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ألّا تكلّم ...) is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the subject آيتك.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «the vocative: ربّ ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl) [Note: The clause may be parenthetical, as a plea for mercy, and the clause اجعل ... is the speech reported.].
The clause «اجعل ...» has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāfiyya bayāniyya).
The clause «آيتك ألّا تكلّم ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported.
The clause «تكلّم ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
11- (الفاء) conjunction; (على قومه) attached to (خرج), and likewise (من المحراب); (الفاء) conjunction; (إليهم) attached to the verb أوحى; (أن) an explicative particle [Note: Or it is a maṣdar-forming particle, and the interpreted maṣdar (أن سبّحوا..) is in the position of accusative as direct object, its governor being أوحى.], (بكرة) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (سبّحوا).
The clause «خرج ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the second clause قال.
The clause «أوحى ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause خرج.
The clause «سبّحوا ...» has no grammatical position, explicative.

* Morphology:
(ليال), plural of ليلة or ليل; and it is said that الليلة is the singular of الليل; a noun for the time extending from sunset to the break of dawn or sunrise; it involves dropping the yāʾ because it is stripped of al- and of annexation, as is the case with the defective noun (manqūṣ).
(سويّا), an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from سوي يسوى, of the pattern-class of fariḥa; its pattern is فعيل, and the yāʾ of فعيل has been assimilated into its third radical.
(بكرة), the noun from بكر إلى الشيء وعليه (to go early to something); its pattern is فعلة with ḍamma then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:12-15.t:
* I'rab:
(يحيى) the one addressed (munādā), a singular proper noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the alif, in the position of accusative; (بقوّة) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of خذ, and (الباء) is for accompaniment (mulābasa); (الواو) resumptive; (الحكم) a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (صبيّا) a ḥāl, accusative, of the object pronoun.
The clause «the vocative: يا يحيى ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied saying, i.e. "Allah the Exalted said: O Yaḥyā..".
The clause «خذ الكتاب ...» has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
The clause «آتيناه ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
13- (الواو) conjunction; (حنانا) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to الحكم [Note: It may be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb.], accusative; (لدن) a noun indeclinable on sukūn in the position of genitive by the preposition, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (حنانا); the last (الواو) is a conjunction — or resumptive —; and the clause «كان تقيّا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause آتيناه — or it is resumptive.
14- (الواو) conjunction; (برّا) conjoined to (تقيّا), accusative; (بوالديه) attached to (برّا), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (الواو) conjunction; (عصيّا) a second khabar (predicate) of the incomplete verb يكن.
The clause «لم يكن جبّارا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause كان تقيّا.
15- (الواو) conjunction; (سلام) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative [Note: The subject came indefinite because it indicates generality, which is the sense of praise.], (عليه) attached to the khabar of the subject; (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to the khabar; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the two verbs (ولد، يبعث) and the fāʿil (agent) of the verb (يموت) is a pronoun referring to Yaḥyā; (حيّا) a ḥāl, accusative, of the deputy agent.
The clause «سلام عليه ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause لم يكن جبّارا. The clause «ولد ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «يموت ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يبعث ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.

* Morphology:
(صبيّا), an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from صبا يصبو, of the pattern-class of naṣara; its pattern is فعيل, and it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by conversion: its original form is صبيو; when the yāʾ and the wāw met in the word with the first of them vowelless, the wāw was converted into a yāʾ and assimilated into the other yāʾ. (حنانا), an aurally-transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb حنّ يحنّ, of the pattern-class of ḍaraba, meaning he was tender and compassionate; its pattern is فعال with fatḥa on the first radical; there is another maṣdar, حنّة, or it is a maṣdar of single occurrence (maṣdar marra).
(تقيّا), an assimilated adjective from the triliteral وقى يقي; its pattern is فعيل, and the yāʾ of فعيل has been assimilated into the third radical of the word. It involves replacing the first radical of the word — the wāw — with a tāʾ, as it is converted before the tāʾ of iftiʿāl, because the wāw is converted into a tāʾ when it comes before the tāʾ of iftiʿāl.
(برّا), an assimilated adjective from برّ يبرّ, of the two pattern-classes of naṣara and ḍaraba; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(عصيّا), an assimilated adjective from عصى يعصي, of the pattern-class of ḍaraba; its pattern is فعيل, and the yāʾ of فعيل has been assimilated into the third radical of the word, which is the yāʾ.

safi-cedvel:16-17.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (في الكتاب) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اذكر); (إذ) an adverbial noun in the position of accusative as a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) of مريم, or of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the story of Maryam"; (من أهلها) attached to (انتبذت); (مكانا) a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, its governor being انتبذت [Note: Or it is an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (انتبذت).].
The clause «اذكر ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive; and the clause «انتبذت ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). 17- (الفاء) conjunction; (من دونهم) attached to a second direct object [Note: Or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of (حجابا), if the verb اتّخذت is made to carry the meaning of أرسلت (she let down) or وضعت (she placed).], (الفاء) conjunction; (إليها) attached to (أرسلنا); (الفاء) conjunction; (لها) attached to (تمثّل); (بشرا) a ḥāl, accusative [Note: What permitted the ḥāl to come as a primitive (jāmid) noun is that it is qualified.], (سويّا) a naʿt (adjective) of (بشرا), accusative.
The clause «اتّخذت ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause انتبذت..
The clause «أرسلنا ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause اتّخذت.
The clause «تمثّل ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause أرسلنا.

* Morphology:
(شرقيّا), a relative adjective (ism mansūb) referring to الشرق, the well-known direction (east); its pattern is فعليّ with fatḥa on the first radical.

safi-cedvel:18-18.t:
* I'rab:
(بالرحمن) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أعوذ); (منك) attached to (أعوذ); (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (كنت) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and (التاء) is its noun; (تقيّا) the khabar (predicate) of كنت, accusative.
The clause «قالت ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «إنّي أعوذ ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أعوذ ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «كنت تقيّا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being "then leave me" or "then keep away from me".

safi-cedvel:19-19.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّما) a restraining particle and the restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (اللام) for causation (taʿlīl); (أهب) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (muḍmara) "an" after the lām, and the fāʿil (agent) is "I"; (لك) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أهب) [Note: The verb وهب takes the second object in the accusative directly: وهبتك المال, or by means of a preposition: وهبت لك المال.], (غلاما) a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (زكيّا) a naʿt (adjective) of غلام, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن أهب..) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (رسول) [Note: Or attached to an implied verb explained by رسول, i.e. "your Lord has sent me to grant ..."].
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «أنا رسول ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أهب ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative.

* Morphology:
(أهب), it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by deletion, for it is the imperfect of the first-radical-weak (mithāl) verb وهب, of the pattern-class of fataḥa; its pattern is أعل with two fatḥas.

safi-cedvel:20-20.t:
* I'rab:
(أنّى يكون لي غلام) its i'rab has already passed [Note: In verse (8) of this sūra.], (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and the second is a conjunction; (أك) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the overt sukūn on the nūn that was dropped for lightness; (بغيّا) the khabar (predicate) of أك, accusative.
The clause «قالت ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يكون لي غلام ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «لم يمسسني بشر ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
The clause «لم أك بغيّا ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause يمسسني.

* Morphology:
(بغيّا), an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from بغت تبغي; the third radical of the word is a yāʾ. It is said its pattern is فعيل, and the feminine tāʾ was not attached to it because it is one of the adjectives particular to females, like حائض and طالق; and it is said it is فعول — a pattern to which the feminine marker is mostly not attached, like صبور — and in that case it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by conversion, since the wāw and the yāʾ met with the first vowelless, so the wāw was converted into a yāʾ and assimilated into the second yāʾ, then the ghayn was given kasra by vowel harmony (itbāʿan).

* Benefits:
1- Interrogative أنّى:
أنّى is interrogative, and it is conditional.
The interrogative one, which is the subject of our discussion, comes with four meanings:
a- In the sense of «من أين» (from where), e.g. «أنّى لك هذا», i.e. "from where do you have this?"
b- It comes in the sense of «كيف» (how), e.g. «أَنَّى شِئْتُمْ»?
c- It comes in the sense of «متى» (when), i.e. "when you wish?"
d- It comes in the sense of «حيث» (wherever), i.e. "wherever you wish". To choose one of the four meanings we go back to the context of the speech. Nothing else ... !

safi-cedvel:21-21.t:
* I'rab:
(قال.. هيّن) its i'rab has already passed [Note: In verse (9) of this sūra.], (الواو) conjunction; (اللام) for causation (taʿlīl); (نجعله) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (muḍmara) "an" after the lām; (آية) a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (للناس) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of (آية); (منّا) attached to an adjective of (رحمة).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن نجعله ...) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "We created him thus in order to make him".
(الواو) resumptive, and the noun of (كان) is a pronoun referring back to the creation understood from the context of the verse; (أمرا) the khabar (predicate) of كان, accusative.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «(الأمر) كذلك ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قال (the second)» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «هو عليّ هيّن ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported.
The clause «(خلقناه) لنجعله ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause هو عليّ هين.
The clause «كان أمرا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(مقضيّا), a passive participle from the triliteral قضى; it is originally on the pattern مفعول, i.e. مقضوي — with a yāʾ at its end — and when the wāw and the yāʾ met with the first vowelless, the wāw was converted into a yāʾ and assimilated into the other yāʾ; then the ḍād was given kasra to suit the yāʾ.

safi-cedvel:22-26.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunction in the two verbs; (به) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of انتبذت, i.e. "carrying him"; (مكانا) a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative — or an adverb of place attached to (انتبذت) [Note: See verse (16) of this sūra.].
The clause «حملته ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to an implied resumptive clause, i.e.:
"So Jibrīl breathed into the opening of her garment, and she felt the pregnancy, and she conceived him."
The clause «انتبذت ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause حملته.
23- (الفاء) conjunction; (إلى جذع) attached to (أجاء), by its being made to carry the meaning of ألجأها (it drove her); (يا) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (ليتني) a particle resembling the verb, for wishing, and (النون) is for protection (wiqāya), and (الياء) a pronoun, the noun of layta; (قبل) an adverb, accusative, attached to (متّ); (هذا) in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) conjunction; (نسيا) the khabar (predicate) of كنت, accusative.
The clause «أجاءها المخاض ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause انتبذت [Note: This is on the view that the conception, the labour and the birth took place within an hour.. It may be resumptive on the view that it took place over nine months.].
The clause «قالت ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «ليتني متّ ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «متّ ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of layta.
The clause «كنت ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause متّ.
24- (الفاء) conjunction, and the fāʿil (agent) of (نادى) is Jibrīl — or ʿĪsā —; (من تحتها) attached to (نادى) [Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl of the agent of نادى.], (أن) an explicative particle [Note: Or it is a maṣdar-forming particle that governs the accusative, and the verb is accusative by the particle, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and لا is then negating; the interpreted maṣdar is genitive by an omitted preposition attached to (نادى), i.e. (بألّا تحزني..).], (لا) prohibitive; (تحزني) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and (الياء) is the agent; (قد) a particle of realization (taḥqīq); (تحتك) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to an omitted second direct object; (سريّا) a first direct object, accusative.
The clause «ناداها ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause قالت.
The clause «لا تحزني ...» has no grammatical position, explicative.
The clause «قد جعل ...» has no grammatical position, giving the reason for the preceding prohibition [Note: Or it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).].
25- (الواو) conjunction; (إليك) attached to (هزّي), by its being made to carry the meaning of أميلي (bend) or قرّبي (bring near); (بجذع) attached to a ḥāl of the object of هزّي — i.e. "shake the fresh dates, being on the trunk of the palm" [Note: Or the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition entering on the object of هزّي.] —, (تساقط) an imperfect verb, jussive as the answer to the request, and the agent is "it", i.e. the palm tree; (عليك) attached to (تساقط); (جنيّا) a naʿt (adjective) of (رطبا).
The clause «هزّي ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause لا تحزني.
The clause «تساقط» has no grammatical position, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, not joined with the fāʾ, i.e. "if you shake.. it will drop".
26- (الفاء) linking an implied apodosis; (عينا) a tamyīz (specification), accusative, converted from the agent; (الفاء) resumptive; «(إمّا) = (إن)» a jussive conditional particle.. and (ما) is redundant; (ترينّ) an imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. — because it is one of the five verbs — and (الياء) an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as agent, and (النون) the nūn of emphasis; (من البشر) attached to a ḥāl of (أحدا), which is a direct object, accusative, its governor being ترينّ; (الفاء) linking the apodosis; (قولي) an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn.. and (الياء) the agent; (للرحمن) attached to (نذرت); (صوما) a direct object, accusative, its governor being نذرت; (الفاء) conjunction; (اليوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (أكلّم). (إنسيّا) a direct object.
The clause «كلي ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you shake and they drop, then eat.." [Note: Or it is conjoined to the clause هزّي, so it too has no grammatical position.]
The clause «اشربي ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause كلي.
The clause «قرّي عينا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause كلي. The clause «إمّا ترينّ ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «قولي ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «إنّي نذرت ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported.
The clause «نذرت ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «لن أكلّم ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause نذرت [Note: Or it is conjoined to the clause of the speech reported, in the position of accusative.].

* Morphology:
(قصيّا), an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from قصا يقصو or قصي يقصى, the first of the pattern-class of naṣara and the second of fariḥa; its pattern is فعيل. If its third radical is a wāw, it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by conversion: its original form is قصيو with a vowelless yāʾ; the yāʾ and the wāw met, the first vowelless, so the wāw was converted into a yāʾ and assimilated into the other yāʾ.. If the third radical is a yāʾ, there is no iʿlāl in it; its pattern is فعيل.
(المخاض), it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of مخضت تمخض الحامل, of the pattern-class of fariḥa, i.e. her delivery drew near and labour pains seized her.. Its pattern is فعال with fatḥa on the first radical, and there is another maṣdar with kasra on the first radical. (جذع), a primitive (jāmid) concrete noun; its pattern is فعل with kasra then sukūn.
(النخلة), the singular of النخل, a noun for the well-known tree (the date palm); its pattern is فعلة with fatḥa then sukūn.
(متّ), it contains a weak-letter change by deletion: a hollow weak verb attached to the agent tāʾ has its second radical dropped; its pattern is فلت with kasra on the first radical, so it is as if it were of the type فعل يفعل, with kasra on the second radical in the past and ḍamma in the imperfect, and so it is anomalous (shādhdh). It is stated in al-Lisān.. «Sībawayh said: it became weak from فعل يفعل with kasra then ḍamma.. and its counterpart among the sound verbs is فضل يفضل with kasra then ḍamma».
(نسيا), a noun for a thing that is forgotten, and for the worthless belongings that travellers leave behind; its plural is أنساء.
(منسيّ), a passive participle from نسي ينسى, of the pattern-class of fariḥa; its pattern is مفعول, and a weak-letter change by conversion has entered it: its original form is منسوي, with a yāʾ at its end preceded by a vowelless wāw; the wāw and the yāʾ met with the first vowelless, so the wāw was converted into a yāʾ and assimilated into the other yāʾ.
(سريّا), a primitive noun for a stream or small river; its pattern is فعيل and its third radical is a yāʾ, because it is from سرى يسري — with a yāʾ at the end of the imperfect — and the yāʾ of فعيل has been assimilated into its third radical; the plural is سريان with kasra on the sīn, like رغيف رغفان.. It may also mean "chief" or "a man of lofty standing", in which case its third radical is a wāw, because it is from سرو يسرو, of the pattern-class of karuma, and it contains a weak-letter change by conversion: its original form is سريو; the yāʾ and the wāw met, the first vowelless, so the wāw was converted into a yāʾ and assimilated into the other yāʾ; and by it ʿĪsā, peace be upon him, is meant.
(رطبا), a collective noun (ism jamʿ) for ripe unripe-dates (busr) before they become dried dates; its pattern is فعل with ḍamma then fatḥa; its singular is رطبة with ḍamma then fatḥa, and the plural is رطاب with kasra on the rāʾ, or أرطاب.
(جنيّا), an assimilated adjective from جنى يجني, of the pattern-class of ḍaraba, and it is what is good and fit for picking; its pattern is فعيل, and the yāʾ of فعيل has been assimilated into the third radical of the word.
(ترينّ), it involves dropping its second radical, which is the hamza, and dropping its third radical, which is the alif; its origin is رأى.. When it was attached to the yāʾ of the feminine addressee, the alif was dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, and it became ترأين.. (then) the vowel of the hamza was transferred to the rāʾ before it, and when two vowelless letters met, the hamza was dropped and it became ترين — this before the entry of the nūn of emphasis — and when the nūn entered, the nūn of the nominative was dropped because of the succession of identical letters [Note: The nūn of the nominative may be dropped in the jussive and the accusative.], and when the vowelless yāʾ of the pronoun met the first vowelless nūn of the heavy nūn of emphasis, the yāʾ of the pronoun was given kasra; the pattern of the verb is تفينّ with two fatḥas then a kasra.
(صوما), an aurally-transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the triliteral صام يصوم, of the pattern-class of naṣara; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(إنسيّا), a relative adjective (ism mansūb) referring to إنس, a generic noun meaning people; its pattern is فعليّ with kasra then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
- Definiteness (al-taʿrīf): In the saying of Allah the Exalted «جِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ».
The definiteness of النخلة is either: the definiteness of names by predominance (al-asmāʾ al-ghāliba), like the definiteness of النجم (the Pleiades) and الصعق, as if in that desert there was a palm trunk well known among the people, so that when "the trunk of the palm" was said, that one was understood and no other palm trunk. Or it is the definiteness of the genus, i.e. the trunk of this tree in particular, as if Allah the Exalted guided her to the palm only in order to feed her fresh dates from it

safi-cedvel:27-28.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (به) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of أتت [Note: I.e. "proud" or "glorying", and its being a particular meaning does not prevent this.], (قومها) a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied (muqaddar) oath; (شيئا) a direct object, accusative, by جئت being made to carry the meaning of فعلت (you did) [Note: Or it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, so it is its kind, i.e. "you have come a strange coming".], (فريّا) a naʿt (adjective) of (شيئا), accusative.
The clause «أتت ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «تحمله ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the agent or of the hāʾ in (به).
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يا مريم and (its answer) ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «جئت ...» has no grammatical position, the answer to the oath, and the oath clause is the answer to the vocative.
28- (أخت) the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative; (هارون) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, for it is a diptote for being a proper name and foreign; (ما) negating in both places.
The clause «the vocative: يا أخت ...» has no grammatical position, a resumption within the scope of the saying.
The clause «ما كان أبوك ...» has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
The clause «ما كانت أمّك ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause answering the vocative.

* Morphology:
(فريّا), an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from فرى يفري, of the pattern-class of ḍaraba, meaning اختلف [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably اختلق, "fabricated", is intended.] or "cut and split"; its pattern is فعيل, and the yāʾ of فعيل has been assimilated into the third radical of the word.

safi-cedvel:29-29.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (كيف) an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (كان) a complete (tāmm) past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "he" [Note: It may be incomplete (nāqiṣa), made to carry the meaning of صار (became) or ما زال (remained), and (صبيّا) is then its khabar (predicate).], and it is the referring pronoun; (في المهد) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (كان); (صبيّا) a ḥāl, accusative, of the agent of كان.
The clause «أشارت ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «كيف نكلّم ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «كان في المهد ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).

safi-cedvel:30-33.t:
* I'rab:
(آتاني) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddara) on the alif..
and (النون) is for protection (wiqāya), and (الياء) a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is "He", i.e. Allah; (الكتاب) a second direct object, accusative; (الواو) conjunction; (جعلني نبيّا) like آتاني الكتاب, and likewise (جعلني مباركا); (أينما) a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis or the protasis; (كنت) a complete (tāmm) past verb ... and (التاء) the agent; (الواو) conjunction; (بالصلاة) attached to (أوصاني); (ما) a maṣdar-forming adverbial particle; (دمت) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb.. and (التاء) its noun; (حيّا) the khabar (predicate) of ما دمت, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ما دمت..) is in the position of accusative as an adverb of time, attached to (أوصاني).
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «إنّي عبد الله ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «آتاني الكتاب ...» has no grammatical position, a resumption within the scope of the saying.
The clause «جعلني نبيّا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause آتاني الكتاب.
The clause «جعلني مباركا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause جعلني نبيّا.
The clause «كنت ...» has no grammatical position, parenthetical.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "wherever I am, He has made me a prophet and blessed".
The clause «أوصاني ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause آتاني.. or جعلني..
32- (الواو) conjunction; (برّا) a second direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being جعلني [Note: I.e. "possessed of dutifulness", with a muḍāf omitted.. or a description by the maṣdar, for intensification.] (بوالدتي) attached to (برّا); (الواو) conjunction; (لم) a particle of negation and jussive; (جبّارا) a second direct object, accusative, its governor being لم يجعلني; (شقيّا) a naʿt (adjective) of (جبّارا), accusative.
The clause «(جعلني) برّا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause جعلني مباركا.
The clause «لم يجعلني ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause (جعلني) برّا.
33- (الواو) conjunction; (عليّ) attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (السلام); (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to the notion of "being established" (al-istiqrār) which is the predicate, and likewise the other adverbs conjoined to it; (حيّا) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «السلام عليّ ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause لم يجعلني.
The clause «ولدت ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «أموت ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أبعث ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.

* Morphology:
(أوصاني), it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by conversion: its original form is أوصيني; the yāʾ was voweled after a fatḥa, so it was converted into an alif; its pattern is أفعلني.

* Benefits:
1- The family of ʿImrān:
Allah chose the family of ʿImrān above the worlds. ʿImrān is the father of Maryam, the mother of the Messiah. We know the striving of the Messiah in calling people to truth, goodness and faith in Allah alone, and we also know how Allah subjected to the Messiah, peace be upon him, disciples — the Ḥawāriyyūn — who spread his religion over many regions of the earth. Allah willed to honour the family of ʿImrān, so He sent down a sūra of the Noble Qur'an named after them, the second sūra after al-Baqara; and He willed to honour the Virgin Maryam, so He singled her out with a sūra of His Noble Book, the sūra we are now dealing with.
I do not think that any of the heavenly books praised the family of ʿImrān, Maryam and the Messiah as the Noble Qur'an did, dwelling at length on their purity and sanctity and on their being free of every defect or calumny.
The Noble Qur'an mentioned that Maryam was a virgin, that the angel gave her the glad tidings of this pure boy, so she conceived him and withdrew from people, and suffered the pains of his delivery until she wished she had died before that; and her son the Messiah addressed her while in his cradle, calmed her fear, and asked her to shake the trunk of the palm and enjoy the fresh ripe dates that would drop upon her.
Maryam's mother was a righteous woman, and her father was a righteous, God-fearing, pure man. His wife vowed her newborn as a servant of the Temple, and when she found it was a female — and the male is not like the female — nevertheless her Lord accepted her with a goodly acceptance and caused her to grow in a goodly way.
2- Why was she prevented from speaking? It is a question that leaps to the mind and then to the tongue. The answer to it is that Allah commanded her to refrain from speaking for two reasons:
a- That ʿĪsā, peace be upon him, should be the one to speak on her behalf, so as to be stronger for her case, a stronger herald of the miracle, and a removal of the factors of suspicion leading to her being accused of something shameful.
b- Pointing out the legal repugnance of disputing with fools; and the poet seized upon this meaning and said:
يخاطبني السفيه بكل قبح ... وأكره أن أكون له مجيبا
(The fool addresses me with every vileness, and I dislike being one who answers him.)

safi-cedvel:34-34.t:
* I'rab:
(ذلك) mubtadaʾ (subject) in the position of nominative; (عيسى) khabar (predicate), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied (muqaddara) ḍamma, and it is denied nunation for being a proper name and foreign; (بن) a naʿt (adjective) of عيسى, nominative [Note: Or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to it, or a badal (substitute) of it.. It may be intended as information, in which case it is a second predicate, and then the alif of ابن must be written.], (قول) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, and it emphasizes the content of the clause before it, i.e. "I say the word of truth" [Note: It may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of عيسى, and it may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "I mean"..], (الذي) in the position of accusative as an adjective of قول; (فيه) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يمترون).
The clause «ذلك عيسى ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يمترون ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).

* Benefits:
1- Writing the alif of «ابن» and dropping it: a- ابن: its origin is «بنو», and it is pluralized as «بنين». Some said: its origin has kasra on the bāʾ, by analogy with «بنت».
b- For non-rational beings, such as «ابن مخاض» (a camel in its second year), «ابن لبون» (a camel in its third year) and ابن عرس (weasel), it is pluralized with alif and tāʾ, like «بنات عرس».
c- ابن is annexed to what specifies it, such as «ابن السبيل» (the wayfarer), «ابن الحرب» (the man of war) and «ابن الدنيا» (the worldly man).
d- The hamza of «ابن» is a connective hamza (hamzat waṣl), and likewise the hamza of «ابنة». It is dropped in connected speech and written in «script».
e- Among its rules is that it is dropped both in pronunciation and in writing, namely when a proper name occurs followed by «ابن» as its adjective, annexed to a proper name that is his father, e.g. «محمد بن عبد الله بن عبد المطلب», except when it occurs at the beginning of a line, in which case the hamza is written but not pronounced.
Remark: by their saying «annexed to a proper name that is his father», what is annexed to a mother of whom he is the son is excluded, such as «عيسى ابن مريم».

safi-cedvel:35-35.t:
* I'rab:
(لله) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of (كان); (ولد) genitive in form, accusative in position, a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being يتّخذ, and the first object is omitted, i.e. "that He should take anyone as a son".
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يتّخذ ...) is in the position of nominative as the postponed noun of كان.
(سبحانه) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb.. and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (إنّما) a restraining particle and the restrained particle (kāffa makfūfa); (كن) a complete (tāmm) imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "you"; (الفاء) conjunction — or resumptive —; (يكون) a complete imperfect verb, nominative, and the agent is "it".
The clause «ما كان لله ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يتّخذ ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «(أسبّح) سبحانه ...» has no grammatical position, parenthetical, of supplication.
The clause «قضى ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. The clause «يقول ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «كن ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «يكون ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause يقول.. or resumptive.

safi-cedvel:36-36.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (ربّي) the khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the letter before the yāʾ.. and (الياء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (ربّكم) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to ربّي by the wāw, nominative; (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (هذا) mubtadaʾ (subject) in the position of nominative; (مستقيم) a naʿt (adjective) of the predicate (صراط).
The clause «إنّ الله ربّي ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied verb, i.e.:
"say".. and the clause of the implied saying has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «اعبدوا ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if you acknowledge His lordship, then worship Him".
The clause «هذا صراط.....» has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).

safi-cedvel:37-37.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (من بينهم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الأحزاب; (الفاء) conjunction; (ويل) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative [Note: Beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted because of the sense of censure in it.], (للذين) attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of the subject (ويل); (من مشهد) attached to the notion of "being established" (al-istiqrār) which is the predicate; (يوم) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive.
The clause «اختلف ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «ويل للذين ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).

* Morphology:
(مشهد), a noun of time, or a noun of place, or a mīm-maṣdar from the triliteral شهد; its pattern is مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm and on the second radical. شهد means "to be present" or "to give testimony".. If it is from the first meaning, the noun of time means the time of being present, the noun of place means the place of being present, i.e. the Standing, and the maṣdar means the being present on that grievous day, by annexation of the maṣdar to its agent. If it is from the second meaning, i.e. testimony, the noun of time means "from the time of the testimony of a day", the noun of place means "from the place of the testimony of a day", and the maṣdar means the testimony of that day, i.e. that the day testifies against people, either literally or figuratively.

safi-cedvel:38-39.t:
* I'rab:
(أسمع) a non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb for expressing wonder (taʿajjub), indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa because it comes in the form of the imperative; (الباء) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (هم) a pronoun whose near position is genitive by the redundant bāʾ and whose remote position is nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of أسمع; (أبصر) like أسمع, and the agent is implied, i.e. أبصر بهم; (يوم) an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أسمع، أبصر); (لكن) a particle of rectification (istidrāk) with no governing effect; (الظالمون) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw; (اليوم) an adverb attached to (ضلال); (في ضلال) attached to the khabar (predicate) of the subject الظالمون.
The clause «أسمع بهم ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أبصر (بهم) ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يأتوننا ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause «الظالمون.. في ضلال ...» has no grammatical position, having the force of a causal clause.
39- (الواو) conjunction, and the pronoun in (أنذرهم) is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (يوم) a second direct object, accusative, on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "warn them of the punishment of the Day of Regret" [Note: It may be an adverb attached to (أنذرهم), with the second object implied.], (إذ) an adverb borrowed for the future, attached to (الحسرة) [Note: Or it is a badal (substitute) of يوم, if (يوم) is parsed as an adverb.], (الأمر) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya) in both places; (في غفلة) attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم); and (لا) negating. The clause «أنذرهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أسمع بهم.
The clause «قضي الأمر ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «هم في غفلة ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object pronoun in (أنذرهم).
The clause «هم لا يؤمنون ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the object pronoun in (أنذرهم).

* Morphology:
(غفلة), an aurally-transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb غفل يغفل, of the pattern-class of naṣara; its pattern is فعلة with fatḥa then sukūn; there are other maṣdars: غفول with two ḍammas and غفل with two fatḥas..

* Rhetoric:
- The mursal trope (al-majāz al-mursal):
In the saying of Allah the Exalted «لكِنِ الظَّالِمُونَ الْيَوْمَ فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ».
The relation is that of the state (ḥāliyya), and what is meant is Hell: the state was mentioned and the place intended, because one does not dwell in error but rather in its place. Likewise His saying in the following verse: «وَهُمْ فِي غَفْلَةٍ»; one does not dwell in heedlessness either, but rather in the places of ruin into which heedlessness casts its people.

* Benefits:
1- The places where the bāʾ is redundant:
The bāʾ is added in six main places:
a- It is added obligatorily to the agent of the verb of wonder in one of its two forms, namely أفعل به, e.g.: «أحسن بعمر» (how good ʿUmar is!); «أحسن» is parsed as a past verb that came in the form of the imperative, and عمر is the agent, nominative by an implied ḍamma whose appearance is prevented by the place being occupied by the vowel of the redundant preposition; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition brought for the harmony of the expression; and of it is «أسمع بهم وأبصر».
It is frequently added to the agent of «كفى» meaning "sufficient", which is an intransitive verb, e.g. «كَفى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيداً»; this is other than كفى meaning "to suffice for" or "to make free of need", for with this the bāʾ is not added to its agent.
b- It is also added to the direct object, e.g.: «وَلا تُلْقُوا بِأَيْدِيكُمْ إِلَى التَّهْلُكَةِ».
And the saying of Allah the Exalted: وهزّي إليك بجزع النخلة. [Translator's note: so printed in the source, with «بجزع» for the Quranic «بجذع».]
c- It is added to the mubtadaʾ, e.g. «بحسبك درهم» (a dirham suffices you), and e.g. خرجت فإذا بزيد (I went out and there was Zayd), and كيف بك «meaning: how are you».
d- It is added to the khabar, and this is analogical (qiyāsī) in the negative case, e.g. «ليس زيد بقائم» (Zayd is not standing) and «وما ربك بغافل»; as for the affirmative, it depends on aural transmission (samāʿ).
e- It is added to the ḥāl when the governor of the ḥāl is negated, e.g.:
فما رجعت بخائبة ركاب ... حكيم بن المسيّب منتهاها
(No riding camels returned disappointed whose journey's end was Ḥakīm ibn al-Musayyab.)
f- It is added in the tawkīd (emphasis) when it is with النفس and العين, e.g.: رأيت خالدا بنفسه وبعينه (I saw Khālid himself).
2- البغيّ:
a- Some said its origin is «بغوي», and al-Bayḍāwī said: its origin is مفعول from البغي; and both have explanations of its transformation into «بغيّ».
b- Some said that «بغيّ» is particular to the feminine, so one says: امرأة بغيّ (an unchaste woman), and one does not say رجل بغيّ.
c- Some objected that it is transmitted from al-Miṣbāḥ that one says: رجل بغيّ and امرأة بغيّ. Perhaps that is by way of analogy and supposition, not from actual usage.

safi-cedvel:64-65.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (ما) negative; the fāʿil (agent) of (نتنزّل) is نحن (we), for glorification, referring to Jibrīl «[Note: or it refers to the angels as a whole, in which case there is no glorification.]»; (إلّا) a particle of restriction; (بأمر) attached to (نتنزّل); (له) attached to an omitted predicate preposed; the relative noun is the mubtadaʾ (subject) postposed; (بين) an accusative adverb attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما; the second relative noun is conjoined to the first; (خلفنا) an accusative adverb attached to an omitted ṣila of the second ما; the third relative noun is conjoined to the first, in the position of the nominative; (بين) like the first, attached to the ṣila of the third ما; (ما) negative.
The clause «ما نتنزّل ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «له ما بين ...» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption.
The clause «ما كان ربّك نسيّا ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause ما نتنزّل.
65- (ربّ) a badal (substitute) for the second ربّك, nominative «[Note: it is possible that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو", and the clause is resumptive.]»; (ما) a relative noun in the position of the genitive, conjoined to السموات by the waw; (بينهما) like the first «[Note: in the preceding verse.]»; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition; (لعبادته) attached to (اصطبر); (هل) a particle of interrogation; (له) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (سميّا) «[Note: or attached to an omitted second direct object of (تعلم).]»; (سميّا) a direct object, accusative.
The clause «اعبده ...» is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you have known His lordship, worship Him."
The clause «اصطبر ...» is in the position of the jussive, conjoined to the clause اعبده.
The clause «تعلم ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive, confirming the lordship.

* Morphology:
(نسيّا): an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) — or an intensive form of the active participle — on the pattern فعيل.
(اصطبر): the tāʾ of the form افتعل has been changed to ṭāʾ because it comes after the ṣād; its origin is اصتبر.

* Benefits:
-
The Messenger ﷺ was asked about the People of the Cave, Dhū al-Qarnayn and the spirit (al-rūḥ), so he asked Jibrīl to inform him about these matters, but Jibrīl delayed the answer to him for fifteen days, and it is said forty, until the polytheists spread the word that his Lord had abandoned him and hated him. Then the revelation came, saying «وَما نَتَنَزَّلُ إِلَّا بِأَمْرِ رَبِّكَ», after He had related to the Messenger the story of the People of the Cave and Dhū al-Qarnayn, and had answered them with a satisfying answer concerning the spirit.

safi-cedvel:66-67.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (الهمزة) for interrogation; (إذا) an indeclinable (mabnī) adverb attached to the omitted answer, the implied form being: "shall I be brought to life" or "shall I be raised" «[Note: it is not permissible to attach it to the verb أخرج, because the lām of ibtidāʾ (commencement) does not allow what follows it to act upon what precedes it, unless we parse the lām as redundant (zāʾida), which is what al-Suyūṭī chose.]»; (ما) redundant; (اللام) the lām of ibtidāʾ; (أخرج) an imperfect passive verb, nominative, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is أنا (I); (حيّا) an emphatic ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative.
The clause «يقول الإنسان ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «the condition, its verb and its apodosis ...» is in the position of the accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «متّ ...» is in the position of the genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «سوف أخرج ...» has no grammatical position; explicative.
67- (الهمزة) for rhetorical denial; (الواو) a conjunction; (لا) negative; (قبل) an adverbial noun, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the genitive, attached to (خلقناه); (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl; (يك) an imperfect verb, jussive, its sign of jussive being the overt sukūn on the nūn, which was dropped for lightening; (شيئا) the khabar of يكن, accusative.
The clause «يذكر الإنسان ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause يقول الإنسان.
The clause «خلقناه ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of أنّ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّا خلقناه ...) is in the position of the accusative, a direct object, its governor being يذكر.
The clause «لم يكن شيئا ...» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl.

safi-cedvel:68-70.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (الواو) the wāw of oath; (ربّك) genitive by the wāw, attached to an omitted verb, the implied form being "I swear"; (اللام) the lām of oath; (نحشرنّهم) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative, and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis and (هم) is a pronoun, direct object, and the fāʿil is نحن (we), for glorification; (الواو) a conjunction; (الشياطين) conjoined to the pronoun of the object, accusative; (ثمّ) a conjunction; (لنحضرنّهم) like لنحشرنّهم; (حول) an accusative adverb attached to (نحضرنّهم); (جثيّا) a ḥāl, accusative.
The clause «(أقسم) بربّك ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «نحشرنّهم ...» has no grammatical position; the answer of the oath.
The clause «نحضرنّهم ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause of the answer of the oath.
69- (ثمّ لننزعنّ) like ثم لنحشرنّ; (من كلّ) attached to (ننزعنّ); (أيّهم) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, a direct object, its governor being ننزعنّ «[Note: this is the view of the majority and of Sībawayh; the relative noun was made indeclinable on the ḍamma because of its annexation to the pronoun and the omission of the beginning of the ṣila (relative clause). But some parsers take the ḍamma as the ḍamma of declension, with several explanations for it:
First: أيّ is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, its khabar being أشدّ, and it is by way of quotation (ḥikāya), i.e. "We shall surely pull out from every faction the group about which it is said: which of them is most intense?" — this is the view of al-Khalīl. Second: like the first, but the clause is the direct object of (ننزعنّ), which is suspended by the interrogative (muʿallaq), its meaning being "We shall surely distinguish", for it has the sense of knowing — this is the view of Yūnus. Third: like the first, but the clause is resumptive and (من) is redundant — this is the view of al-Akhfash, who permits the redundancy of من in an affirmative context. ... And there are other explanations by al-Mubarrad and al-Farrāʾ, involving some artificiality.]»; (أشدّ) the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو"; (على الرحمن) attached to (عتيّا), which is a tamyīz (specification), accusative.
The clause «ننزعنّ ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause نحضرنّهم.
The clause «(هو) أشدّ ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (أيّ).
70- (اللام) the lām of oath; (بالذين) attached to (أعلم), the khabar; (بها) attached to (أولى); (صليّا) a tamyīz, accusative.
The clause «نحن أعلم ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause ننزعنّ. And the clause «هم أولى ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).

* Morphology:
(جثيّا): the plural of جاث, an active participle from جثا يجثو on the pattern فاعل. Its yāʾ, which had been converted from a wāw, was dropped — because what precedes it is kasra — dropped because it met the sukūn of the tanwīn as a silent letter. And جثيّ has a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by conversion: its origin, after the preceding change, is جثوي on the pattern قعود; the wāw and the yāʾ came together with the first silent, so the wāw was converted to yāʾ and merged with the second yāʾ; then the thāʾ was given kasra to suit the yāʾ... then the jīm was given kasra by adjacency.
(صليّا): a regular maṣdar of the verb صلي يصلى (the pattern of فرح), on the pattern فعول, and its origin is صلوي; the wāw and the yāʾ came together with the first silent, so the wāw was converted to yāʾ and merged with the other yāʾ; then the lām was given kasra to suit the yāʾ, and the ṣād was given kasra by adjacency.

* Rhetoric:
- The art of the oath (fann al-qasam):
In His saying, Exalted is He, «فَوَ رَبِّكَ لَنَحْشُرَنَّهُمْ».
This art is: the speaker wishes to swear about something, so he swears by that in which there is pride for him and magnification of his standing, or praise of his worth, or that which is a disparagement of another, or which runs in the manner of amatory tenderness, or which comes out in the manner of admonition and asceticism.
In this oath there are two matters: one, the confirmation of the report; the second: that in Allah the Exalted swearing by His name — sanctified be His names — annexed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, there is an exaltation of the standing of the Messenger of Allah and an elevation of him, just as He elevated the standing of the heaven and the earth in His saying, Exalted is He, «فَوَ رَبِّ السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ».

* Benefits:
- The disagreement of the grammarians about «أيّهم»:
al-Kisāʾī was asked: why is it not permissible for us to say «أيهم قام»? He said: «أي كذا خلقت», i.e. "thus I was set up". And what Abū al-Baqāʾ said about «أيّهم»: he said: it is read أيّهم with the accusative and it is read with the ḍamma, and there are two views on it:
a- that it is a ḍamma of indeclinability: this is the school of Sībawayh, and it was made indeclinable because it has the meaning of الذي. b- The second view: that it is a ḍamma of declension; and in this view there are five aspects.
1- That it is a mubtadaʾ and أشد is its khabar.
2- The second: that it is a mubtadaʾ and khabar and interrogative.
3- أيّ is interrogative and من is redundant.
4- That «أيّهم» is nominative by the word شيعة.
5- That «ننزع» is suspended from acting (ʿulliqat), because the meaning of the sentence is the meaning of a condition, and a condition does not act upon what precedes it. The implied form is: "whether they were partisans or were not partisans." And this is the furthest of the five from correctness..!

safi-cedvel:71-72.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive — or a conjunction; (إن) a particle of negation; (منكم) attached to a preposed khabar (predicate) «[Note: or it is an naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "إن أحد منكم", and the khabar is (واردها).]»; (إلّا) a particle of restriction «[Note: it may be for exception if the speech before it is taken as complete, i.e. "منكم أحد" — a preposed khabar and a postposed mubtadaʾ (subject) — and then (واردها) is a badal (substitute) for أحد.]»; (واردها) a postposed mubtadaʾ, nominative; and the ism (noun) of (كان) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو", i.e. the arrival (al-wurūd) understood from the context; (على ربّك) attached to (مقتضيّا), which is an naʿt of the khabar of كان; (حتما) accusative.
The clause «إن منكم إلّا واردها» has no grammatical position; resumptive «[Note: or conjoined to the clause نحن أعلم.. so it falls within the scope of the answer of the oath in His saying: فو ربك لنحشرنّهم.]».
The clause «كان.. حتما ...» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption — or causal.
72- (فيها) attached to (جثيّا), which is a second direct object «[Note: it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) if (نذر) has the meaning "We leave them"; and it may be that the preposition and its noun are attached to a ḥāl from الظالمين or to (نذر).]».
The clause «ننجّي ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause إن منكم..
The clause «اتّقوا ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «نذر ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause ننجّي.

* Morphology:
(حتما): a samāʿī (heard-pattern) maṣdar of the triliteral verb حتم, on the pattern فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
- Iltifāt (shift of address):
In His saying, Exalted is He, «وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وارِدُها».
It may be a resumption of address to the people, and it may be an iltifāt.
The possibility of iltifāt is based on intending generality in the first, so that those addressed first are those addressed second, except that the first address is in the wording of the absent person and the second in the wording of the present person. But if we build on the view that the first was intended only as particular, on both assumptions, then the second is not an iltifāt, but a turning to a specific address to particular people.

* Benefits:
أي: "ayy" comes here as an interrogative noun, by which the specification of a thing is sought, like His saying, Exalted is He: «أَيُّ الْفَرِيقَيْنِ خَيْرٌ مَقاماً وَأَحْسَنُ نَدِيًّا» -

safi-cedvel:73-73.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (عليهم) attached to (تتلى); (بيّنات) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, its sign of the accusative being the kasra; (للذين) attached to (قال); (أيّ) an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, its khabar (predicate) being (خير), nominative; (مقاما) a tamyīz (specification), accusative; (أحسن) conjoined to خير, nominative; (نديّا) a tamyīz, accusative.
The clause «تتلى ... آياتنا» is in the position of the genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «قال الذين ...» has no grammatical position; the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (الذين).
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «أيّ الفريقين ...» is in the position of the accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

* Morphology:
(نديّا): a noun with the meaning of النادي (the assembly), on the pattern فعيل, with a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by conversion; its origin is نديو, for its lām is a wāw, from (ندوتهم، أندوهم), i.e. "I came to their assembly".. the wāw and the yāʾ came together with the first silent, so the wāw was converted to yāʾ and merged with the other yāʾ.

safi-cedvel:74-74.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (كم) khabariyya (declarative), a metonym for a large number, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative, a preposed direct object; (قبلهم) an accusative adverb attached to (أهلكنا); (من قرن) the tamyīz (specification) of كم; (هم) a detached pronoun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being أحسن; (أثاثا) a tamyīz, accusative.
The clause «أهلكنا ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «هم أحسن أثاثا ...» is in the position of the genitive, an naʿt (adjective) of قرن.

* Morphology:
(رئيّا): an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from رأى, on the pattern فعل with kasra then sukūn, with the meaning of المرئيّ (the seen), like ذبح with the meaning of المذبوح (the slaughtered).

* Benefits:
- «من» entering upon the tamyīz.
There is a disagreement about this «من»: some made it partitive, and therefore it does not enter upon what is not divisible into parts. Some said it is redundant, and this is the opinion of Sībawayh, and for this reason «منتقبا» was conjoined in the accusative to the position of the tamyīz and not to its wording.
Ibn Hishām and al-Zamakhsharī said it is to show the genus, so it cannot be redundant, because it is not added in other than an affirmative context. So reflect and choose — may you be guided to what is correct.

safi-cedvel:75-75.t:
* I'rab:
(من) a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative, a mubtadaʾ (subject); (في الضلالة) the khabar (predicate) of كان; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of the condition; (اللام) the lām of command; (له) attached to (يمدد); (مدّا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative; (حتّى) a particle of commencement; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, a direct object; (يوعدون) an imperfect passive verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (إمّا) a particle of division and apportioning; (العذاب) a badal (substitute) for ما, accusative, and likewise (إمّا الساعة), conjoined to it; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of the condition; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, a direct object «[Note: or an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause: هو شرّ مكانا, and the interrogative clause is in the position of the accusative, a direct object of (يعلمون), which is suspended from direct action by the interrogative.]»; (مكانا) a tamyīz, accusative; (أضعف) conjoined to شرّ, nominative; (جندا) a tamyīz, accusative.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «من كان ...» is in the position of the accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «كان.. فليمدد» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «يمدد له الرحمن ...» is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of the condition, accompanied by the fāʾ.
The clause «رأوا ...» is in the position of the genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «يوعدون ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «سيعلمون ...» has no grammatical position; the apodosis of a non-jussive condition, and the clause «هو شرّ ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (من).

* Morphology:
(مدّا): a samāʿī (heard-pattern) maṣdar of the triliteral verb مدّ, on the pattern فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(أضعف): a noun of preference (ism tafḍīl) from the triliteral ضعف, on the pattern أفعل.
(جندا): a generic collective noun with the meaning of "army" (ʿaskar); its singular is جنديّ, and its plurals are أجناد and جنود; and the pattern of جند is فعل with ḍamma then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
- Orderly laff and nashr (enfolding and unfolding):
In His saying, Exalted is He, «شَرٌّ مَكاناً وَأَضْعَفُ جُنْداً».
Where the first refers back to «خَيْرٌ مَقاماً», and the second to «وَأَحْسَنُ نَدِيًّا».

safi-cedvel:76-76.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (اهتدوا) a past verb, indeclinable on an implied ḍamma on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two silent letters.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent); (هدى) a second direct object, accusative; (الواو) a conjunction; (عند) an accusative adverb attached to (خير); (ثوابا) a tamyīz (specification), accusative, and likewise (مردّا).
The clause «يزيد الله ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «اهتدوا ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «الباقيات.. خير......» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.

* Morphology:
(مردّا): a mīmī maṣdar from the triliteral ردّ, on the pattern مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm and on the ʿayn.

* Benefits:
- A kind of preference (tafḍīl):
«الْباقِياتُ الصَّالِحاتُ خَيْرٌ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ ثَواباً وَخَيْرٌ مَرَدًّا». There is no believer who does not know that the enduring good deeds are all good, so what is the import of the preference in this verse?
The answer is that this kind of preference resembles our saying: "Summer is more intense in heat than winter" — the comparison here is not between the heat of summer and the heat of winter, but between the intensity of heat and the intensity of cold. So reflect, for there is an extremely subtle meaning in the matter.
