There is another opinion on the content of this verse, which is that the preference came in the manner of mushākala (conformity), which often occurs in the verses of the Qur'an, and which we have treated in more than one place in this book.

safi-cedvel:77-80.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for astonished interrogation; (الفاء) resumptive; (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, a direct object; (بآياتنا) attached to (كفر); (اللام) the lām of oath, for an implied oath; (أوتينّ) an imperfect passive verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative, and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنا"; (مالا) a direct object, accusative.
The clause «رأيت ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «كفر ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause of the ṣila.
The clause «أوتينّ ...» has no grammatical position; the answer of the implied oath.. and the clause of the oath and its answer is in the position of the accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
78- (الهمزة) for interrogation; (أم) a conjunction equivalent to the interrogative hamza; (عند) an accusative adverb attached to an omitted second direct object; (عهدا) a first direct object, accusative.
The clause «اطّلع ...» is in the position of the accusative, a second direct object of the verb (رأيت) in the sense of "you informed".
The clause «اتّخذ ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause اطّلع.
79- (كلّا) a particle of deterrence and rebuke; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, a direct object; (الواو) a conjunction; (له) attached to (نمدّ); (من العذاب) attached to (نمدّ) «[Note: or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from (مدّا).]»; (مدّا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative.
The clause «سنكتب ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive, containing the sense of causation.
The clause «يقول ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «نمدّ ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause نكتب.
80- (الواو) a conjunction; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, a badal ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) for the pronoun in (نرثه), i.e. "We shall inherit what he has of wealth and children" «[Note: or it is a direct object of the verb نرث, and the attached third-person pronoun is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "We shall inherit from him what he says.." — said by al-ʿUkbarī. And if the verb نرث is made to include the meaning "We deprive" or "We strip", then (ما) is a second object of the verb.]»; (الواو) a conjunction; (فردا) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, i.e. "alone" (munfaridan).
The clause «نرثه ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause نكتب.
The clause «يقول ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يأتينا ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause نكتب.

* Morphology:
(فردا): a rigid (jāmid) noun with the meaning "one", on the pattern فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
- Majāz ʿaqlī (rational figurative usage):
In His saying, Exalted is He, «سَنَكْتُبُ ما يَقُولُ».
That is, "We shall command the angels to write" — so it is an ascription of a thing to its cause.

safi-cedvel:81-82.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (من دون) attached to an omitted second direct object; (آلهة) a first direct object, accusative; (اللام) the lām of causation; (يكونوا) a defective imperfect verb, accusative, its sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is a pronoun, the ism (noun) of يكون.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يكونوا ...) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (اتّخذوا).
(لهم) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (عزّا), which is the khabar (predicate) of يكونوا, accusative.
The clause «اتّخذوا ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «يكونوا ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (أن).
82- (كلّا) a particle of deterrence and rebuke, and the pronoun of the fāʿil (agent) in (سيكفرون) refers to the gods (āliha); (بعبادتهم) attached to (يكفرون), and the third-person pronoun that is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) refers to the polytheists, or refers to the gods; (الواو) a conjunction; (عليهم) attached to a ḥāl from (ضدّا), which is the khabar of يكونون, accusative.
The clause «يكفرون ...» has no grammatical position; in the status of a causation for the deterrence.
The clause «يكونون ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause يكفرون.

* Morphology:
(عزّا): a samāʿī (heard-pattern) maṣdar of the triliteral عزّ, used as an intensive description, on the pattern فعل with kasra then sukūn.
(ضدّا): an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from ضدّ يضدّ (the pattern of نصر), on the pattern فعل with kasra then sukūn; it has come in the verse indicating a plural entity, i.e. "enemies", and ضدّ is a plural in the wording of the singular.

* Benefits:
- «كلّا» and its six views.
a- The majority of the Basrans did not take it out of being a particle of deterrence and rebuke, and perhaps this is what accords with the places where it occurs in the Noble Qur'an.
b- al-Kisāʾī and those who sided with him see that it has the meaning of «حقّا» (truly).
c- The view of ʿAbd Allāh al-Bāhilī is that it is a rejection of what precedes it. And this agrees with "rebuke and deterrence".
d- As for the saying of Abū Ḥātim, it is a "particle of opening" (ḥarf istiftāḥ).
e- al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl held that it is a particle of affirmation with the meaning of "yes" (naʿam), and there is something to consider in this.
And there is a sixth opinion, that it is a filler (ṣila) in the speech, and there is also something to consider in this.
And if you reflect, you will find the first opinion to be the one in use for this particle, and what is other than it is little used, and perhaps weak.

safi-cedvel:83-87.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for interrogation; (تر) an imperfect verb, jussive, its sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; (على الكافرين) attached to (أرسلنا); (أزّا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّا أرسلنا..) is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the two objects of ترى.
The clause «لم تر ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «أرسلنا ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of أنّ..
The clause «تؤزّهم ...» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الشياطين, i.e. "inciting them to acts of disobedience", or from الكافرين, i.e. "moved toward acts of disobedience".
84- (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition; (لا) prohibitive, jussive; (عليهم) attached to (تعجل); (إنّما) kāffa and makfūfa (restrainer and restrained); (لهم) attached to an omitted ḥāl from (عدّا), which is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative.
The clause «لا تعجل ...» is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if they fall into disobedience, do not hasten the punishment against them".
The clause «نعدّ ...» has no grammatical position; causal.
85- (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (نعدّ) «[Note: or it is a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" (remember).]»; (إلى الرحمن) attached to (وفدا), which is an accusative ḥāl from المتّقين, with the meaning "arrivers" (wāfidīn).
The clause «نحشر ...» is in the position of the genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
86- (الواو) a conjunction; (إلى جهنّم) attached to (نسوق); (وردا) an accusative ḥāl from المجرمين, i.e. "coming to the watering place" (wāridīn).
The clause «نسوق ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause نحشر.
87- (لا) negative; (إلّا) a particle of exception; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as a disconnected (munqaṭiʿ) exception «[Note: or a connected one if the pronoun of (يملكون) refers to المتّقين.. or it is a badal (substitute) for the fāʿil of يملكون, in the position of the nominative.]»; (عند) an accusative adverb attached to an omitted second direct object; (عهدا) a first direct object, accusative.
The clause «لا يملكون ...» is in the position of the accusative, a second ḥāl from المجرمين «[Note: or it is disconnected, resumptive, with no grammatical position.]»,

* Morphology:
(أزّا): a maṣdar of أزّ يؤزّ (the pattern of نصر) and of أزّ يئزّ (the pattern of ضرب), on the pattern فعل with fatḥa then sukūn; and there are other maṣdars: أزيز with fatḥa on the hamza, and أزاز with fatḥa on it.
(عدّا): a samāʿī maṣdar of the verb عدّ يعدّ (the pattern of نصر), on the pattern فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(وفد): a collective noun or the plural of وافد, which is one who approaches a place; the plural of وفد is وفود; and the pattern of وفد is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(وردا): a collective noun with the meaning of الواردين or it is a plural of وارد, on the pattern فعل with kasra then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:88-91.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (ولدا) a second direct object.. and the first object is implied, i.e. (عزيزا) according to the Jews, or (عيسى) according to the Christians, or (الملائكة) according to some of the Arabs.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «اتّخذ الله ...» is in the position of the accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
89- (اللام) the lām of oath, for an implied oath; (قد) a particle of confirmation; (شيئا) a direct object, accusative, by including in جئتم the meaning of فعلتم «[Note: or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, being its kind, i.e. "an abominable coming".]»; (إدّا) an naʿt (adjective) of (شيئا), accusative.
The clause «جئتم ...» has no grammatical position; the answer of the implied oath.
90- (منه) attached to (يتفطّرن); (هدّا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, so it meets it in meaning, accusative «[Note: or it is a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl, i.e. "demolished".]».
The clause «تكاد السموات ...» is in the position of the accusative, an naʿt of (شيئا); the clause «يتفطّرن ...» is in the position of the accusative, the khabar (predicate) of تكاد.
The clause «تنشقّ الأرض.....» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause يتفطّرن.
The clause «تخرّ الجبال ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause يتفطّرن.
91- (أن) a maṣdar particle; (دعوا) a past verb, indeclinable on an implied ḍamma on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two silent letters.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent); (للرحمن) attached to (دعوا); (ولدا) a direct object, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن دعوا ...) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted causal lām, attached to the three verbs: يتفطّرن, وتنشقّ and تخرّ, i.e. "because they ascribed..." «[Note: according to Abū Ḥayyān, the difference of the agent between the verb and the interpreted maṣdar prevents making it a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) in the position of the accusative.]».
The clause «دعوا ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(إدّا): an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from أدته الداهية تؤدّه (with ḍamma) and تئده (with kasra) and تأده (with fatḥa), "the calamity overwhelmed him", on the pattern فعل with kasra then sukūn. And الإدّ is the calamity or the great matter, and the plural is إداد with kasra on the hamza, and إدد with kasra on it.
(هدّا): a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral verb هدّ (the pattern of نصر), or the pattern of ضرب, in which case it is intransitive with the meaning "it collapsed", on the pattern فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
- Iltifāt (shift of address):
In His saying, Exalted is He, «لَقَدْ جِئْتُمْ شَيْئاً إِدًّا» — this speech is a rejection of their false statement, and a magnification of its gravity, by way of iltifāt from the absent person to address, which announces the perfection of anger and the intensity of wrath, and discloses the utmost of condemnation and denunciation, and records against them the extreme of impudence, ignorance and audacity.

safi-cedvel:92-93.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (ما) negative; (للرحمن) attached to (ينبغي); (يتّخذ ولدا) like its counterpart «[Note: in verse (88) of this sūra.]».
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يتّخذ ولدا) is in the position of the nominative, the fāʿil (agent) of ينبغي.
The clause «ما ينبغي ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «يتّخذ ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative.
93- (إن) a particle of negation; (كلّ) a mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (في السموات) attached to an omitted ṣila of من; (إلّا) a particle of restriction; (آتي) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ كلّ, nominative, its sign of the nominative being an implied ḍamma on the yāʾ; (الرحمن) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (عبدا) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in آتي, accusative.
The clause «كلّ من ... آتي» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption — or causal.

safi-cedvel:94-95.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) the lām of oath, for an implied oath; (وعدّا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative.
The clause «أحصاهم ...» has no grammatical position; the answer of the implied oath.. and the clause of the implied oath is resumptive.
The clause «عدّهم ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause أحصاهم.
95- (الواو) a conjunction; (كلّهم) a mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, its khabar (predicate) being آتيه; (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (آتيه); (فردا) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from the pronoun in آتيه.
The clause «كلّهم آتيه» ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause of the answer of the oath.

safi-cedvel:96-96.t:
* I'rab:
(السين) a particle of futurity; (لهم) attached to (يجعل) «[Note: or attached to an omitted second direct object of the verb جعل in the sense of "made into".]»; (ودّا) a direct object, accusative.
The clause «إنّ الذين آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «عملوا ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause of the ṣila.
The clause «سيجعل.. الرحمن ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(ودّا): a samāʿī (heard-pattern) maṣdar of the verb ودّ (the pattern of فرح), on the pattern فعل with ḍamma then sukūn.. and the verb has other maṣdars: ود with fatḥa and kasra on the wāw, and وداد with fatḥa, kasra and ḍamma on the wāw, and ودادة with fatḥa on the wāw, and مودّة with fatḥa on the mīm, and موددة with kasra on the first dāl and fatḥa on the second and fatḥa on the mīm, and مودودة.

safi-cedvel:97-97.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) causal; (إنّما) kāffa and makfūfa (restrainer and restrained); (بلسانك) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the third-person hāʾ; (اللام) for causation; (تبشّر) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; (به) attached to (تبشّر).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تبشّر) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (يسّرناه).
(الواو) a conjunction; (تنذر به قوما) like تبشّر به المتّقين; (لدّا) an naʿt (adjective) of (قوما), accusative.
The clause «يسّرناه ...» has no grammatical position; a causation for an implied statement, i.e. "convey what has been sent down, for We have only made it easy".
The clause «تبشّر ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «تنذر ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause تبشّر.

* Morphology:
(لدّا): the plural of ألدّ on the pattern أفعل, an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from لدّ يلدّ (the pattern of نصر), i.e. "he disputed with intense disputation", and the pattern of لدّ is فعل with ḍamma then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:98-98.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (كم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن) its parsing has already been given «[Note: in verse (74) of this sūra.]»; (هل) a particle of interrogation for denial; (منهم) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (أحد) — an naʿt (adjective) that has been preposed before the described; (أحد) genitive in wording, accusative in position, a direct object of the verb تحسّ; (أو) a conjunction; (لهم) attached to a ḥāl from (ركزا), which is a direct object whose governor is تسمع, accusative.
The clause «أهلكنا ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «تحسّ ...» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption «[Note: it may be in the position of the genitive, an naʿt of قرن, the clause being declarative in meaning.]».
The clause «تسمع ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause تحسّ.

* Morphology:
(ركزا): a noun for the faint sound or sensation, on the pattern فعل with kasra then sukūn.

* Benefits:
- The interrogative and the declarative كم:
We spoke earlier about كم in its two kinds at length, and now we return and mention these two kinds briefly, for the sake of reminder only.
a- The interrogative: that by which an indefinite number is signified, whose specification is sought, such as: كم كتابا قرأت (How many books have you read?).
b- The declarative: that by which a large number is signified, by way of reporting, such as: كم مرة نصحناهم فلم ينتصحوا..! (How many times we advised them, yet they did not take advice..!)

safi-cedvel:40-40.t:
* I'rab:
(نحن) a detached pronoun borrowed for the position of the accusative, to emphasise the attached pronoun in إنّا [Note: it is permissible that it be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause نرث, and the nominal clause is the khabar of inna.] (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, conjoined to الأرض by the wāw (عليها) attached to an omitted element, the ṣila of من (إلينا) attached to (يرجعون), an imperfect passive verb.. and (الواو) is the deputy agent.
[Translator's note: the source entry begins at this point; the beginning of the i'rab of the verse is not present in the text.]
The clause «إنّا.. نرث.....» has no grammatical position; it is a resumptive clause giving a reason.
The clause «نرث ... » is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of inna.
The clause «يرجعون ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive.

safi-cedvel:41-45.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (في الكتاب) attached to a ḥāl from إبراهيم (نبيّا) a second khabar, accusative.
[Translator's note: the source text of this entry is abridged at the beginning; the parsing of the first words of the verses is not present in it, and it is translated as written.]
The clause «اذكر ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «إنّه كان صدّيقا ... » is in the position of the accusative, as a ḥāl from إبراهيم [Note: or it is parenthetical between the badal and the one substituted for, if إذ is parsed as a badal of "the account of Abraham" with an omitted muḍāf.. or an explanatory resumption.].
The clause «كان صدّيقا ... » is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of inna.
42- (إذ) an indeclinable adverb, attached to (صدّيقا نبيّا) [Note: or it is a badal of إبراهيم with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "mention the account of Abraham when he said".], (لأبيه) attached to (قال), and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ (أبت) the one addressed, muḍāf, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the bāʾ, and (التاء) is redundant, a compensation for the yāʾ of the first person that is omitted, with no grammatical position..
and the omitted (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi (لم) a preposition and an interrogative noun in the position of the genitive, attached to (تعبد), and the alif is dropped from ما because the preposition enters it (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, mafʿūl bihi (لا) negative in the three places (عنك) attached to (يغني) (شيئا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative [Note: or it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, i.e. "something of avail".], i.e. something of benefit or harm.
The clause «قال ... » is in the position of the genitive, as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «the vocative and its response ... » is in the position of the accusative, as the reported speech.
The clause «لم تعبد ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause «لا يسمع ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «لا يبصر ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يسمع.
The clause «لا يغني ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يبصر.
43- (قد) a particle of confirmation (من العلم) attached to (جاءني), and مِن is partitive [Note: it is permissible that it be attached to an omitted ḥāl from (ما), which is an indefinite described noun.], (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, agent of جاءني (يأتك) an imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the agent is "he", and it is the returning pronoun, and (الكاف) is mafʿūl bihi (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition (أهدك) an imperfect verb, jussive as the response to a request, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the agent is "I" (صراطا) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (سويّا) naʿt of صراط, accusative.
The clause «يا أبت ... » has no grammatical position; it is a resumption within the scope of the saying.
The clause «إنّي قد جاءني ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative..
The clause «جاءني.. ما لم يأتك ... » is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of inna.
The clause «لم يأتك ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «اتّبعني ... » is in the position of the jussive, as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you want guidance, follow me"..
The clause «أهدك ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of an implied condition, not accompanied by the fāʾ.
44- (لا) a prohibitive. (تعبد) was given a vowel, the kasra, because of the meeting of two sākin letters, and the agent is "you" (للرحمن) attached to (عصيّا), the khabar of كان.
The clause «يا أبت ... » has no grammatical position; it is a resumption within the scope of the saying.
The clause «لا تعبد ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause «إنّ الشيطان كان ... » has no grammatical position; it gives a reason.
The clause «كان للرحمن عصيّا ... » is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of inna. 45- (عذاب) agent of يمسّك, nominative (من الرحمن) attached to a naʿt of (عذاب).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يمسّك..) is in the position of the accusative, as mafʿūl bihi, whose governor is أخاف.
(الفاء) a conjunction (تكون) an incomplete imperfect verb (a governing verb), accusative, conjoined to (يمسّك), its noun a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you" (للشيطان) attached to (وليّا), the khabar of تكون, accusative.
The clause «يا أبت ... » has no grammatical position; it is a resumption within the scope of the saying.
The clause «إنّي أخاف ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause «أخاف ... » is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of inna.
The clause «يمسّك عذاب ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
The clause «تكون ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila of the particle-type relative.

* Benefits:
1- The logic of Abraham in argumentation:
It was the reader's due from us that we present to him a sketch of the life of Abraham, but we have postponed that to another place, and preferred to present to him a picture of Abraham's way in counsel and guidance. These verses have drawn the attention of many exegetes, because of the beauty of style in them, the gradualness of the counsel, the gentleness toward the father, and the many courtesies of argumentation.
We have before us texts of the great exegetes concerning what these verses contain of ways of presenting ideas and eloquence of style, and we have preferred to choose the best of them and present them to the reader, as a witness to what we are about, and as its confirmation. Al-Zamakhsharī says at length, and it would be well if the reader savoured and took it in: «Look when he wished to counsel his father and admonish him about the great error in which he was entangled, and the shameful deed in which he disobeyed the command of the intelligent and stripped himself of the matter of discernment, and of the stupidity beyond which there is no stupidity: how he arranged the speech with him in the finest order, and drove it along the most graceful course, using courtesy, gentleness, kindness and mildness, fine manners and good character, taking counsel in that from the counsel of his Lord, Mighty and Exalted. That is that he first asked him for the reason of his error, an asking that alerts him to his persistence and wakes him from his excess and extremity; for if the object of worship were alive, discerning, hearing, seeing, able to reward and punish, beneficial and harmful, yet only one of the creatures, he who judged it fit for worship and described it with lordship would be deemed light-minded, and it would be recorded against him as manifest misguidance and great wrong, even if it were the noblest of creatures and the highest of them in station; so what do you suppose of one who directs his worship to an inanimate thing, without sense or awareness, which does not hear, O worshipper of it, your mention of it and your praise of it, nor see the postures of your submission and humility, let alone avail you, by your asking it to ward off an affliction so that it wards it off, or a need arising for you so that it suffices you in it...!
Then he followed with his call to the truth, gently and kindly with him; he did not name him with extreme ignorance nor himself with surpassing knowledge, but said: with me is a portion of knowledge, something of it that is not with you, and that is knowledge of directing to the even path, so do not disdain; suppose that you and I were on a journey, and I had knowledge of the guidance and you did not, then follow me, I will save you from going astray and wandering...!
Then he added a third, by deterring and forbidding him from what he was in, in that the Satan who rebelled against your Lord, the Merciful, from whom comes all that you have of blessings, is your enemy who wants for you nothing but every destruction, disgrace and punishment, and the enemy of your father Adam and of all your kind; and he is the one who entangled you in this error and commanded you to it and made it attractive to you, so that, if you examine closely, you are a worshipper of Satan...!
Yet Abraham, peace be upon him, because of his going deep into sincerity and the loftiness of his aspiration in lordship, mentioned of the two offences of Satan only the one that concerns specifically the Lord of Might, namely his disobedience and arrogance, and did not turn to mention his enmity to Adam and his offspring; as if reflection on the greatness of what he had committed in that had submerged his thought and covered his mind.
Then he added a fourth, by frightening him with the evil of the outcome and with the consequence and calamity that what he is in draws after it; and this was not devoid of fine manners, since he did not state plainly that the punishment would reach him and that the torment would cling to him, but said: "I fear that a punishment from the Merciful will touch you"; so he mentioned fear and touching, and mentioned punishment, and made the guardianship of Satan and entering the number of his followers and friends greater than the punishment; for the good pleasure of Allah is greater than the reward itself, and Allah the Exalted named it as what is witnessed for as the great triumph; so likewise the guardianship of Satan, which is the opposite of Allah's good pleasure, is more severe and greater than the punishment itself.
And he opened each of the four counsels with his saying: «يا أَبَتِ»
as a means of approach to him and an appeal for sympathy.. The old man turned to him with the harshness of unbelief and the coarseness of stubbornness, and called him by his name, and did not answer his «يا أَبَتِ»
with «يا بني», and he put the khabar before the mubtadaʾ in his saying: «أَراغِبٌ أَنْتَ» because it was more important to him, and in it is a kind of wonder and denial at Abraham's desire for his gods.»
End of al-Zamakhsharī's words in this section of the story of Abraham with his father, and the story of the smashing of the people's idols, and the story of his being thrown into the fire and the story of his deliverance from it, when Allah made it coolness and safety for him. After that comes his departure from his country in eastern Iraq and his emigration for the sake of his religion to the land of Canaan in Palestine.
2- يا أَبَتِ
:
We return to speak about the dropping of the yāʾ of the first person in some cases, and we single out here «يا أبت ويا أمت». There are dialects regarding the yāʾ of the first person in the vocative, and as for the tāʾ in «يا أبت ويا أمت» there are two views:
One is that this tāʾ is the tāʾ of the feminine, like the tāʾ in خالة and عمة, and this is the view of Sībawayh and al-Khalīl b. Aḥmad.
The second is that this tāʾ is a compensation for the omitted yāʾ of the first person. The origin is: يا أبي and يا أمي; the yāʾ was dropped because the kasra indicates it, then this tāʾ was given as a compensation for the yāʾ, and so we do not say: يا أبتي and يا أمتي, lest we combine the compensation and the thing compensated.
Although the first view belongs to two pillars of grammar and language, I am at ease with the second and prefer it to the first; as for you, O reader, choose of the two what seems preferable to you and what your taste and opinion decide. And Allah is the Granter of success.

safi-cedvel:46-46.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for interrogation (راغب) mubtadaʾ, nominative [Note: what justified beginning with an indefinite is its dependence on an interrogative.], (أنت) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, agent of the active participle, which takes the place of the khabar [Note: it is permissible that the pronoun be a postponed mubtadaʾ and (راغب) a fronted khabar.], (عن آلهتي) attached to (راغب), (اللام) the lām that prepares for an oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam) (إن) a conditional particle that jussively governs (تنته) an imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the agent is "you" (اللام) the lām of the oath (أرجمنّك) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative.. and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis, and (الكاف) is mafʿūl bihi, and the agent is "I" (الواو) a conjunction (مليّا) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to the verb (اهجرني), or it is a ḥāl from the agent of اهجرني if the meaning is "enjoying your life", i.e. safe, or a mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. "a long forsaking".
The clause «قال ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «أراغب أنت ... » is in the position of the accusative, as the reported speech.
The clause «the vocative: يا إبراهيم ... » has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical.
The clause «لم تنته ... » has no grammatical position; it is a resumption within the scope of the saying.
The clause «أرجمنّك ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the oath.. and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath.
The clause «اهجرني ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied clause caused by his saying لأرجمنّك.. i.e. "so beware of me and forsake me for a long while".

* Morphology:
(مليّا): either a noun indicating a long time, or a derived assimilated adjective from ملا يملو said of the camel, meaning "it travelled hard and ran", and it was borrowed for length of life; so it is on the pattern فعيل.. and it contains iʿlāl by substitution: its origin is مليو; the yāʾ and the wāw met, the first being sākin, so the wāw was turned into a yāʾ and assimilated into the other yāʾ.

safi-cedvel:47-48.t:
* I'rab:
(سلام) mubtadaʾ, nominative [Note: beginning with an indefinite is sound because of the sense of supplication in it.], (عليك) attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (السين) a particle of futurity (لك) attached to the verb أستغفر (بي) attached to (حفيّا), the khabar of كان, accusative.
[Translator's note: the source entry gives only the parts of the i'rab listed here for verse 47; the other words of the verse are not parsed in it.]
The clause «قال ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «سلام عليك ... » is in the position of the accusative, as the reported speech [Note: or it has no position, being parenthetical, and the clause أستغفر is the reported speech, in the position of the accusative.].
The clause «سأستغفر ... » has no grammatical position; it is a resumption within the scope of the saying.
The clause «إنّه كان ... » has no grammatical position; it gives a reason.
The clause «كان بي حفيّا ... » is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of inna.
48- (الواو) a conjunction in the three places (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the pronoun of the addressee in (أعتزلكم) (من دون) attached to a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun, i.e. "what you call upon as an object of worship besides Allah" (عسى) a complete past verb whose agent is the interpreted maṣdar (ألّا أكون..) in the position of the nominative, (بدعاء) attached to (شقيّا), which is the khabar of أكون, accusative.
The clause «أعتزلكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause سأستغفر..
The clause «تدعون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «أدعو ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أعتزلكم..
The clause «عسى ألّا أكون ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption [Note: or it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of أدعو, i.e. "hoping that I will not be wretched in calling"].
The clause «أكون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).

safi-cedvel:49-50.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive (لمّا) an adverb meaning "when", containing the sense of a condition, attached to the apodosis وهبنا (ما يعبدون من دون الله) the i'rab of its like has been given [Note: in the preceding verse (48).], (له) attached to (وهبنا) [Note: the verb وهب takes the second object without a preposition or by means of a preposition, namely the lām.], (الواو) circumstantial (كلّا) a fronted mafʿūl bihi (نبيّا) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, whose governor is جعلنا.
The clause «اعتزلهم ... » is in the position of the genitive, as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يعبدون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «وهبنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «جعلنا ... » is in the position of the accusative, as a ḥāl with an implied قد [Note: or it has no position, being conjoined to the clause وهبنا.].
50- (الواو) a conjunction (لهم) attached to (وهبنا) (من رحمتنا) attached to (وهبنا) (لهم) the second, attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi whose governor is جعلنا (لسان) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (عليّا) naʿt of لسان, accusative.
The clause «وهبنا لهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause وهبنا له.
The clause «جعلنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause وهبنا لهم.

* Rhetoric:
1- Majāz mursal (unrestricted figurative usage):
in His saying, the Exalted «وَجَعَلْنا لَهُمْ لِسانَ صِدْقٍ عَلِيًّا».
Its relation is causation, like the hand for a gift; and the "tongue of the Arabs" is their language. It is also applied to a splendid message, as in the saying of al-Aʿshā al-Bāhilī: إنني أتتني لسان لا أسرّ بها ("A message has come to me with which I am not pleased").
2- Kināya (allusion) in His saying, the Exalted: «وَجَعَلْنا لَهُمْ لِسانَ صِدْقٍ عَلِيًّا»: He alluded to fair mention and beautiful praise by the tongue, because praise is by the tongue; hence He said «لِسانَ صِدْقٍ», just as giving is alluded to by the hand.

safi-cedvel:51-53.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (اذكر.. مخلصا) the i'rab of its like has been given [Note: in verse (41) of this sūra.], (الواو) a conjunction (نبيّا) a second khabar of كان, accusative.
The clause «اذكر ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «إنّه كان مخلصا ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «كان مخلصا ... » is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of inna.
The clause «كان رسولا ... » is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause كان مخلصا.
52- (الواو) a conjunction (من جانب) attached to (ناديناه) (نجيّا) ḥāl, accusative, from the accusative pronoun in (قرّبناه).
The clause «ناديناه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause إنّه كان مخلصا.
The clause «قرّبناه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause ناديناه.
53- (الواو) a conjunction (وهبنا.. رحمتنا) the i'rab of its like has been given [Note: in verse (50) of this sūra.], (أخاه) the first mafʿūl bihi, whose governor is وهبنا, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the alif (هارون) ʿaṭf bayān — or a badal of أخاه — accusative; it is prevented from tanwīn because it is a proper name and foreign (نبيّا) ḥāl, accusative, from (أخاه).
The clause «وهبنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause قرّبناه.

safi-cedvel:54-55.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (اذكر.. نبيّا) the i'rab of its like has been given [Note: in verse (41) of this sūra.].
The clause «اذكر.....» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «إنّه كان صادق ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «كان صادق ... » is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of inna.
The clause «كان رسولا ... » is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause كان صادق.
55- (الواو) a conjunction (بالصلاة) attached to (يأمر) (عند) an adverb, accusative, attached to (مرضيّا), which is the khabar of كان, accusative.
The clause «كان يأمر ... » is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause كان صادق..
The clause «يأمر ... » is in the position of the accusative, as khabar of كان.
The clause «كان.. مرضيّا» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause كان صادق.

* Morphology:
(مرضيّا) a passive participle of the triliteral verb رضي, and it contains iʿlāl by substitution twice: first, the wāw was turned into a yāʾ in the verb, its origin being رضو — with a kasra on the ḍād — because its maṣdar is الرضوان; when the ḍād took the kasra the wāw was turned into a yāʾ, and it became رضي.. second, the wāw was turned into a yāʾ in the passive participle, its origin being مرضوي; the wāw and the yāʾ met, the first being sākin, so the wāw was turned into a yāʾ and assimilated into the other yāʾ.

safi-cedvel:56-57.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (اذكر.. نبيّا) the i'rab of its like has been given [Note: in verse (41) of this sūra.].
The clause «اذكر ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «إنّه كان صدّيقا ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «كان صدّيقا ... » is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of inna.
57- (الواو) a conjunction (مكانا) an adverb, accusative, attached to (رفعناه) (عليّا) naʿt of (مكانا), accusative.
The clause «رفعناه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause إنّه كان.

* Morphology:
(إدريس): a foreign proper name; its pattern, by Arabic analogy, is إفعيل, with a kasra on the hamza.

* Rhetoric:
- Istiʿāra (metaphor):
in His saying, the Exalted «وَرَفَعْناهُ مَكاناً عَلِيًّا».
He likened the great standing and the lofty rank to a high place, by way of istiʿāra.

safi-cedvel:58-58.t:
* I'rab:
(أولئك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ (الذين) khabar of the mubtadaʾ [Note: it is permissible that the relative be a naʿt of the demonstrative — or a badal, or ʿaṭf bayān — and the khabar then becomes the following condition with its verb and its apodosis: إذا تتلى ...], in the position of the nominative, (عليهم) attached to (أنعم), (من النبيّين) attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in (عليهم), (ذريّة) a badal of النبيّين, with the preposition repeated (ممّن) attached to what (من ذريّة) is attached to; so it is conjoined to it, (مع) an adverb, accusative, attached to (حملنا), (من ذريّة إبراهيم) attached to what (من ذريّة آدم) is attached to; so it is conjoined to it, and likewise (ممّن..) is conjoined to it also (إذا) an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, attached to the apodosis خرّوا (تتلى) an imperfect passive verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma (عليهم) attached to (تتلى), (سجّدا) ḥāl, accusative, from the agent of خرّوا (بكيّا) conjoined to سجّدا, accusative.
The clause «أولئك الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «أنعم الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «حملنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the first relative noun (من).
The clause «هدينا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (من).
The clause «اجتبينا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause هدينا.
The clause «تتلى.. آيات ... » is in the position of the genitive, as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «خرّوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.

* Morphology:
(بكيّا): plural of باك, an active participle of بكى; and in بكيّ there is iʿlāl by substitution: its origin is بكوي, like قعود, plural of قاعد; the wāw and the yāʾ met, the first being sākin, so the wāw was turned into a yāʾ and assimilated into the other, then the kāf was given a kasra to suit the yāʾ.

safi-cedvel:59-62.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive (من بعدهم) attached to (خلف) by giving it the sense of "came" (خلف) agent of خلف, nominative (الشهوات) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition (سوف) a particle of futurity (غيّا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «خلف.. خلف ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «أضاعوا ... » is in the position of the nominative, as naʿt of خلف.
The clause «اتّبعوا ... » is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause أضاعوا.
The clause «سوف يلقون ... » is in the position of the jussive, as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if they are presented for reckoning, they will meet…"
60- (إلّا) a particle of exception [Note: it is in the sense of لكن according to al-Suyūṭī, so the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), and (من) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause أولئك يدخلون, and the fāʾ is redundant because of the mubtadaʾ's resemblance to a condition; Abū Ḥayyān chose the connected (muttaṣil) exception.], (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, as the excepted (صالحا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (الفاء) resumptive (أولئك) a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is the clause يدخلون (لا) negative (يظلمون) an imperfect passive verb..
and (الواو) is the deputy agent (شيئا) mafʿūl bihi, by giving يظلمون the sense of "they are diminished", i.e.:
something of the reward [Note: or a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, i.e.: "they are not wronged any wrong".].
The clause «تاب ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «آمن ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تاب.
The clause «عمل ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause آمن.
The clause «أولئك يدخلون ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يدخلون ... » is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
The clause «لا يظلمون ... » is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause يدخلون [Note: it is permissible that it be parenthetical between the badal (جنّات) and the one substituted for (جنّة).].
61- (جنّات) a badal of الجنّة, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra (التي) a relative noun in the position of the accusative, naʿt of جنّات, (بالغيب) attached to a ḥāl from عباد, i.e. "believers in the unseen", or from the omitted returning pronoun, i.e. "the Garden, while it is absent from them"; and the pronoun in (إنّه) either refers to الرحمن, or it is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn).
The clause «وعد الرحمن ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (التي).
The clause «إنّه كان وعده ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «كان وعده مأتيّا» is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of inna.
62- (فيها) attached to (يسمعون), (لغوا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (إلّا) a particle of exception (سلاما) accusative as a disconnected exception (الواو) a conjunction (لهم) attached to a fronted khabar (رزقهم) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative (فيها) attached to the omitted khabar (بكرة) an adverb of time attached to the "being fixed" (istiqrār) that is the khabar.
The clause «لا يسمعون ... » is in the position of the accusative, as a ḥāl from جنّات عدن [Note: or it is cut off as a resumption and has no position.].
The clause «لهم رزقهم ... » is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause لا يسمعون.

* Morphology:
(مأتيّا): a passive participle of the triliteral verb أتى, and it contains iʿlāl by substitution: its origin is مأتوي; the wāw and the yāʾ met in the word, the first being sākin, so the wāw was turned into a yāʾ and assimilated into the other yāʾ, and the tāʾ was given a kasra to suit the yāʾ.
(بكرة): a noun in the sense of al-ghudwa (early morning); its pattern is فعلة.. and see verse (11) of this sūra.

* Rhetoric:
- Emphasising praise by what resembles blame, and the reverse (tawkīd al-madḥ bi-mā yushbih al-dhamm):
in His saying, the Exalted «إِلَّا سَلاماً».
It is a disconnected exception, and salām is either in its well-known meaning, i.e. "but they will hear the greeting of the angels to them, 'Peace upon you'", or the greeting of some of them to others; or in the sense of speech free of fault, i.e. they will hear speech free of fault and deficiency, and this is of the emphasis of praise by what resembles blame, as in the poet's saying:
ولا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم ... بهن فلول من قراع الكتائب
(Gloss: "There is no fault in them except that their swords are notched from the clashing of the battalions.")
It conveys the negation of hearing idle talk by the strongest, demonstrative way. And the connection (the exception being connected), on this view, is by way of supposition and estimation; without that it would not fall into its place of beauty and exaggeration.

safi-cedvel:63-63.t:
* I'rab:
(تلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable on the overt sukūn on the yāʾ that is dropped because of the meeting of two sākin letters, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ (الجنّة) a badal of تلك, nominative (التي) a relative in the position of the nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ [Note: the relative noun came as khabar without a pronoun of separation because الجنّة has been mentioned before in the preceding verses.], (من عبادنا) attached to a ḥāl from the following relative (من) — a naʿt that has been put before what it describes — (من) a relative, mafʿūl bihi of نورث, in the position of the accusative.
The clause «تلك الجنّة التي ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «نورث ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (التي).
The clause «كان تقيّا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).

* Morphology:
(نورث): the hamza is dropped here for lightness; its past is أورث, and the origin would be to say نؤورث, but the hamza was found heavy in utterance, so it was dropped.

* Rhetoric:
- Istiʿāra (metaphor):
in His saying, the Exalted «تِلْكَ الْجَنَّةُ الَّتِي نُورِثُ مِنْ عِبادِنا».
That is: "We leave the Garden to him, as We leave to the heir the property of the testator", and because the God-fearing will meet their Lord on the Day of Resurrection when their deeds have ended and their fruit remains, namely the Garden; so when He admits them to the Garden, He has made them inherit from their God-fearing, as the heir inherits property from the deceased.
He has thus borrowed inheritance for the granting of the Garden.
